title: Basic types and literals
intro: TypeScript's basic types describe the JavaScript values you already use — strings, numbers, booleans — plus special types for absence (null, undefined), safety (any, unknown, never), and precision (literal types). This module teaches which type to pick, how they compare to C# built-ins, and when to prefer unions over enums.

flowchart LR

  B --> C["any, unknown, never ladder"]
  C --> D["Literal types and as const"]
  D --> E["type vs interface"]
  E --> F["Enums and union alternatives"]
  F --> G["TypeScript vs C# mapping"]

conceptCards.title: One number type
conceptCards.summary: TypeScript has string, number, boolean, bigint. number is always IEEE 754 double — no int or decimal like C#.

conceptCards.title: Two absent values
conceptCards.summary: null is intentional absence; undefined is missing/unassigned. strictNullChecks makes them explicit in unions.

conceptCards.title: any → unknown → never
conceptCards.summary: any disables checking. unknown requires narrowing. never is the bottom type for exhaustiveness.

conceptCards.title: Literal types and as const
conceptCards.summary: const infers exact values. as const deep-freezes objects to readonly literals. Derive unions from const objects.

conceptCards.title: type vs interface
conceptCards.summary: type for unions, tuples, and mapped types. interface for object contracts, extends, and declaration merging.

conceptCards.title: Enums vs unions
conceptCards.summary: Numeric enums generate run-time objects with reverse mapping. Prefer as const objects + literal unions for new code.

conceptCards.title: C# type mapping
conceptCards.summary: C# int/decimal/double → TS number (with caution). C# null → TS null. Types erase at emit — validate JSON at boundaries.
conceptCards.example: Serialize decimal as string or integer cents.

revisionDiagram.title: TypeScript basic types concept map
revisionDiagram.source:
mindmap
  root((Basic Types))
    Primitives
      string immutable
      number IEEE 754 double
      boolean true/false
      bigint large ints
    Absence
      null intentional
      undefined missing
      void no return
      never impossible
    Safety ladder
      any unchecked
      unknown must narrow
      never bottom type
    Literals
      const inference
      as const freeze
      discriminated unions
    Naming
      type alias unions
      interface objects
      declaration merging
    Enums
      numeric IIFE
      string enum
      const enum inline
      union alternative
    C# interop
      decimal to cents
      enum validation
      type erasure
